inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: They’re using France’s new “psychological subjection” law to make an example of Father Bernard Domini, the abbot who leads the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame. The official framing may sound like protection, but a vague law like this gives institutions a powerful tool to decide which beliefs and communities are acceptable. The conviction should worry anyone who values religious freedom or civil liberties: once authorities can define “subjection,” they can use that language to silence groups they find inconvenient.
